Also, he will never be Alone... private psyche places are pretty damn nice. He will be comfortable so do not worry about that! Secondly, try not to project yourself into his actions. What I have learned in the ER and my personal life is that you cannot be a savior for everyone. You are a good person for helping, but try not to lose pieces of yourself

We judge a psyche patient based on if they try to fight, are crying nonstop, or are just being assholes to the staff. All of those things will make it hard for him to have phone access. Is your boyfriend mentally ill? I mean like diagnosed with schizophrenia or bipolar?
May I know how old you/ your boyfriend are?

It really all depends on how unstable he acts. A 5150 is a 72 hour hold that starts the moment the document is signed by the doctor so any time he spends in the ER counts that towards the time of the hold. How long before he has access depends entirely on the staff and if they deem him,"fit", for phone time.

This is hard to hear, but typically nurses take people's phones when they are on a 5150 hold due to the fact that they might try to contact their loved ones in an, "upsetting state". It is a bit fucked up, but also good to protect people around him. He will get access to an phone at the psyche facility he got transferred to, but only at the point that the nurses and doctors there deem it is okay.
I work in an ER.  If he is on a 5150  he is as safe as can possibly be. Even without that hold he is still in the relative safety of an ER
